what: The mass is 126.0 ± 0.4 (stat) ± 0.4 (sys) GeV. A result holds one interval, so the systematic component survives only in the claim's text; the numbers cannot be combined or compared by machine.

Exclusion ranges (111-122, 131-559 GeV at 95% CL) have no point value. A result without value is refused (rule 66), so they had to become a table of range bounds, losing that they are confidence statements at 95%.
A particle and its decay modes are neither methods, populations nor concepts; they went to kind `other`.
Significance in standard deviations and p0 are ordinary results, but whether a significance is local or global, and over which range, can only be said in the variable's text.
Energy and integrated luminosity are conditions every number depends on; condition values cannot carry units, so they live in the definitions' text.
No place for the event selection, signal regions, background estimation, systematic uncertainty breakdown, or the HEPData record and likelihoods that would let a reader recompute.
Thousands of authors credited as 'The ATLAS Collaboration'. Fine for a converted paper; a native paper could not list the collaboration as a contributor.

The validator warns that 0.4 and 0.3 in the statements match no recorded number: the symmetric uncertainties (±0.4 stat, ±0.4 sys; ±0.3) can only be recorded as interval bounds, and the second component not at all.
Stating the excluded ranges in the claim is what physicists read; the format pushes them into a table and asks for the 'pattern' instead. Acceptable, but the ranges are the finding.
Restricted by a collaboration's data policy: no reason value fits (`other`).
